paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**Answer.**
From the sources consulted: 28 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 16 manhole overflow, 7 sewer backup, 5 street flooding [nyc311].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.

Checks run: citations and numbers on every claim; lead rules on the answer; no entailment check needed, since the answer is the cited text word for word.

documents.sandy_inundation: This address sits within the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM).
documents.fema_nfhl: This address sits in FEMA flood zone AE (a Special Flood Hazard Area), per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970184F, effective 2007.
documents.dep_moderate_2050: This address is outside the modeled flooding in the NYC DEP stormwater scenario (2.13 in/hr, 2050 SLR).
documents.ida_hwm: No Hurricane Ida (Sept 2021) high-water marks were surveyed within 800 m of this address. Nearest USGS-surveyed mark: Visitation Pl., between Van Brunt St. and Richards St., Red Hook, Brooklyn (3155 m away).
documents.floodnet: 1 FloodNet community sensor within 600 m has logged 2 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years. 1 of the sensors that logged events is flagged by FloodNet for maintenance, so its depths are not used for the peak.
documents.nyc311: 28 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 16 manhole overflow, 7 sewer backup, 5 street flooding.
documents.nycha_development_exposure: 1 flood-exposed NYCHA development within 2000 m of this address (the register lists only developments found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every development): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise).
